generatedCommentsNodes.comment: In `assertTestCaseResultAndWarnings`, when the `result` is an `Iterable`, the subsequent assertions comparing the `result` object itself to `Double.NaN` or `Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY` (e.g., `assertThat(result, not(equalTo(Double.NaN)))`) are redundant and logically ineffective, as a collection will never be equal to a `Double` value.

The method `assertTestCaseResultAndWarnings` uses Java language assertions (e.g., `assert testCase.getMatcher().matches(Double.NaN) == false;`). These are typically disabled by default in JVMs unless the `-ea` flag is explicitly passed. To ensure these checks always run during tests, they should be replaced with framework-specific assertions such as `assertThat(...)` or `assertTrue(...)`.

The refactoring of test case generation into the `addSuppliers` helper method introduces a regression in test coverage. The previous implementation using `randomList(minRows, maxRows, ...)` allowed for the creation of empty lists (size 0) when `minRows` was 0. The new logic only generates lists of size 1 (`<single ...>`) or sizes between 2 and `maxRows` (`<...s>`). This removes critical boundary condition testing for empty input sets across all functions using this supplier.
